comparisons.peer_topic: Fair value hedges of fixed-rate indebtedness
comparisons.peer_summary: Fair value hedges use interest rate contracts to hedge changes in fair value of fixed-rate indebtedness, with gains/losses recognized in current earnings primarily in interest and other, net, and cash flows classified in financing activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC disclose the use of interest rate swaps specifically designated as fair value hedges to mitigate exposure to changes in the fair value of fixed-rate debt resulting from benchmark interest rate fluctuations. Both companies recognize the gains or losses on these hedges in current earnings (interest expense), which offset the corresponding gains or losses on the hedged fixed-rate debt. MU reports that the impact was not significant for 2024, whereas INTC describes the recognition mechanics generally without providing a specific 2024 dollar impact for this specific hedge program in the cited text.

sentences.text: We also utilize fixed-to-floating interest rate swaps designated as fair value hedges to minimize certain exposures to changes in the fair value of fixed-rate debt that result from fluctuations in benchmark interest rates.
We also recognized offsetting reductions in interest expense of the same amounts related to the changes in the fair value of the hedged portion of the underlying debt for these periods.

Fair value hedges use interest rate contracts, such as interest rate swaps, to hedge against changes in the fair value on certain of our fixed-rate indebtedness attributable to changes in the benchmark interest rate.

The gains or losses on these hedges, as well as the offsetting losses or gains related to the changes in the fair value of the underlying hedged item attributable to the hedged risk, are recognized in earnings in the current period, primarily in interest and other, net.
